primary_meaning: Consecration and divine empowerment by the Holy Spirit, setting a person apart for sacred office, service, or mission
primary_basis: 1 Samuel 16:13 (David anointed; Spirit of the Lord comes upon him)
Isaiah 61:1 and Luke 4:18 (Spirit of the Lord upon me because he has anointed me)
Acts 10:38 (God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power)
Exodus 30:22-33; Leviticus 8 (priestly consecration with holy anointing oil)
1 John 2:20, 27 (believers have an anointing from the Holy One)

alternatives.meaning: Physical healing or restorative care (oil as medicinal/sacramental agent)
Joy, abundance, or festive blessing (oil of gladness)
Specific identification of Jesus as the Messiah/Christ (the Anointed One) and the fulfillment of royal/priestly office
Hospitality, honor, or refreshment toward a guest

notes: Across historic Christian interpretation the core symbolic cluster is consecration plus Spirit-empowerment; christological use (Jesus as the Anointed) is especially fixed. Secondary associations with healing, joy, or hospitality are well-attested but context-dependent rather than competing primary meanings. No major confessional tradition treats the term as symbolically unsettled.
